description: The Node Contract: what a node IS, independent of how it is implemented or where it runs. This is a DEFINITION, not a Node Registry implementation — P6 implements the registry, this fixes the shape it must honour. The central promise: a node's identity never changes because its implementation changed.
identityRule: A node is identified by `type` + `typeVersion`. Neither may change because the implementation, runtime or language changed. A workflow referencing `n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest@4` keeps working whether that node is served by the JS compatibility runtime today or a prebuilt Rust artifact later.

identity.typeVersion: integer node version, as upstream n8n uses
identity.displayName: human label — presentation only, never identity

parameters.dynamic: whether options are resolved at edit time (P7 dynamic-parameters)
parameters.credentialsRefs: parameter paths that reference a credential

io.inputs: declared input ports and their data shapes
io.outputs: declared output ports and their data shapes
io.binary: whether binary data is produced or consumed

credentials.required: credential type ids this node needs
credentials.optional: credential type ids it can use
credentials.rule: A node declares credential TYPES. It never reaches into credential storage — resolution is the credentials domain's job, passed in at execution.

execution.operationClass: one of the foundation operation classes (atomic/best-effort/retryable/compensatable)
execution.cancellable: must honour deadline + cancellation from the envelope
execution.streaming: whether output is a STREAM (and then its backpressure policy)

descriptor.events: events the node emits during execution (progress, partial output, log)

errors.rule: Errors use stable codes from the LEGO error contract, namespaced `node.*` or the node's own declared namespace. Display text is never the identity — the frontend owns presentation, which is what keeps a future Translation LEGO possible.

capabilities.rule: Requested explicitly and granted explicitly. A node's trust level never implicitly grants a capability.

descriptor.portability: one of the foundation portability profiles

runtimeRequirements.runtimes: which runtimes can serve this node (js-compat | rust-native | wasm | remote-worker)

creationRoutes.rule: Twelve legitimate ways a node can come into existence. P2.8-B defines route IDENTITY, use, compatibility, cost, portability, security and migration rules ONLY — none of the routes is implemented here. The future AI Node Creator picks among them.

routes.name: No-code API node
routes.use: a REST API wrapped by configuration alone
routes.security: no code execution; only the declared endpoints are reachable
routes.migration: trivially re-describable; the cheapest route to keep

routes.name: Declarative node
routes.use: n8n's declarative style: routing described as data
routes.security: no arbitrary code; the safest executable route
routes.migration: portable across runtimes because it carries no host assumptions

routes.name: OpenAPI → node
routes.use: generate a node from an OpenAPI/Swagger document
routes.security: inherits the declarative route's safety; the spec URL is an input, not a runtime dependency
routes.migration: regenerate from the spec rather than hand-patching

routes.name: Visual node builder
routes.use: a node assembled in a UI by a non-programmer
routes.security: no free-form code; output is data

routes.name: Transform / formula node
routes.use: pure data transformation via an expression
routes.implementation: expression evaluated in a restricted evaluator
routes.security: restricted evaluator: no network, filesystem or subprocess
routes.migration: the strongest Rust/WASM candidate — pure, deterministic, hot

routes.name: Workflow as node
routes.use: an existing workflow reused as a single node
routes.security: inherits the capabilities of the nodes inside it — never more
routes.migration: no migration: it is composition, not code

routes.name: JavaScript / TypeScript node
routes.use: arbitrary logic, and the entire existing n8n ecosystem
routes.implementation: JS module implementing the node interface
routes.security: restricted compatibility environment; capabilities granted explicitly
routes.migration: may later be re-implemented behind the SAME Node Contract in Rust/WASM without changing node identity

routes.name: Python node
routes.use: data/ML work where the Python ecosystem is decisive
routes.migration: usually stays Python — rewriting loses the ecosystem that justified it

routes.name: WASM node
routes.security: sandboxed by construction — the best default for untrusted compute
routes.migration: ships prebuilt; no toolchain on the user device

routes.name: Rust native node
routes.use: hot paths where CPU/memory cost is material
routes.security: native access is powerful — reserved for core/verified code
routes.migration: MUST ship prebuilt per platform. Requiring a compiler on a user device is forbidden.

routes.name: Remote node
routes.use: execution that cannot or should not happen on this device
routes.implementation: the same contract invoked over a real process/network boundary
routes.security: a genuine trust boundary: authenticate, authorise, and never forward raw secrets
routes.migration: what lets a constrained device keep a heavy node in its catalog

routes.name: Existing community node
routes.use: reuse what the n8n ecosystem already has
routes.migration: PROTECTED. Community nodes must keep loading unchanged; adopting the Node Contract must never be a precondition for working.

decisionModel.summary: How a future AI Node Creator picks a route. Inputs are measurable, weights are explicit, and the rule set is small enough to audit.

rules.when: an existing community node already does it
rules.because: zero implementation and zero maintenance beat any rewrite

rules.when: it is a REST API wrapper
rules.because: no code means no attack surface and no upgrade cost

rules.when: it is a pure, hot, deterministic transform
rules.because: this is where native speed is actually material

rules.when: portability or sandboxing matters more than peak speed
rules.because: one prebuilt artifact runs everywhere, isolated

rules.when: the device is constrained and the work is heavy
rules.because: the catalog should not shrink on a phone

rules.when: the Python ecosystem is the reason it exists

rules.because: it is the ecosystem default and always compatible

neverBecause: another component is written in Rust
hardConstraints: must ship prebuilt per platform — never require a compiler on a user device
must implement the SAME Node Contract, with the same identity and error codes
must not break JS or community-node compatibility
must be replaceable back to JS if it regresses

decisionModel.tieBreak: When two routes score equally, choose the one with the lower total lifecycle cost: maintenance + upgrade + scale-out, not implementation time.

lifecycle.quarantineRule: Quarantine is MANDATORY as a concept: a node that fails validation, breaks at runtime, or violates its declared capabilities is quarantined — kept installed and inspectable, but not loaded — rather than silently deleted or left running.

requirements: package scope so two packages cannot collide
dependency conflicts detected at install, not at execution
a package lock so an install is reproducible
isolation.rule: One community package must never be able to silently destabilise another.

compatibilityMatrix.rule: The matrix is what turns the decision model from opinion into lookup. P2.8-B defines the dimensions and seeds them from the route table; P6 populates it per installed node.

compatibilityPromise: Existing n8n community nodes keep loading. The compatibility runtime is the default, not a fallback.
Node identity (`type` + `typeVersion`) never changes because of a migration, a runtime change or a reimplementation. A saved workflow that referenced a node must keep resolving it.

The migration path is one-directional and optional: JS node -> Node Contract descriptor -> compatibility runtime -> (much later, only if justified) an alternative implementation behind the same contract.
A node author is never required to adopt the Node Contract. Adoption buys better metadata, capability declarations and portability information; it is not a condition of running.
No community node is ever rewritten in Rust in order to keep working. Rust is an optional additional implementation, never a requirement.
A node whose package fails verification is quarantined, never silently disabled and never deleted before the cause is recorded.
